response.query: Which MR sequences and physics factors (FLAIR, T2, T1, PD, noise, bias, coil, motion, partial voluming) give the largest reduction in sim‑to‑real gap for lesion detection in brain MRI?
response.answer: FLAIR and T2 sequences, along with advanced denoising and bias correction techniques, provide the largest reduction in the sim-to-real gap for lesion detection in brain MRI. Deep learning methods further enhance these sequences for better accuracy.

results.content: The rise in DL technology has dramatically improved the performance of MR image quality enhancement methods for better medical image analysis through denoising and bias field correction (Zhang *et al* 2017). To identify, compile, and summarize different state-of-the-art (SOTA) DL-based brain MRI enhancement methods for noise removal by denoising, bias field effect removal, motion correction, and their effectiveness in image analysis tasks. | 3D-Parallel-Rician-Net (Wu *et al* 2021) | Combined local and global information assessment-based MRI denoising model with dilated CNN residual learning with large receptive \_elds and learn from the channel data and location information | Limited experimentation on simulated T1-W MRI and require pair of high-quality ground-truth and noise free images |. | Inception-ResNet (Pawar *et al* 2022) | DL-based fully 3D motion simulator for large training datasets, validates simulated and real motion affected MR images in real clinical settings | Effectively suitable for 2D MRI slices, produce different results in each orientation view plane for each 2D slice |.
